transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-05
Start Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alicia Romero (Redwood AE), Devon Cho (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Cobalt Hollow - Head of Infra), Liam O'Connor (Cobalt Hollow - Security), Jenna Ruiz (Cobalt Hollow - PM)

Auto-generated summary (may be rough):
Cobalt Hollow is evaluating Redwood for a mixture of hosted and private deployments. Primary gating items: SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO via SAML, RBAC and tenant isolation, audit logs retention and format, and KMS/encryption integration and key ownership. They are leaning toward dedicated or private deployment due to data residency and regulatory concerns but want to validate cost/latency tradeoffs and operational model. Next step is sharing security pack and setting up a demo tenant with logs.

Topics: SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, data retention, VPC/private control plane, dedicated capacity sizing

Transcript:
[00:00] Alicia: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick intro, I'm Alicia, AE on Redwood, and with me is Devon, our solutions engineer. How are you folks doing?
[00:08] Maya: Doing good, thanks. We're short staffed this week so appreciate the time.
[00:11] Liam: Yep, hi. We wanted to focus mostly on security controls today, and like, how keys and logs are handled.
[00:18] Alicia: Perfect, that's what we wanted to surface. Quick agenda: compliance badges (SOC2/ISO), SSO and SAML flow, RBAC and tenant isolation, audit trail details and retention, and KMS options (customer-managed keys, HSM). Sound right?
[00:30] Jenna: Yes please, and also we're concerned about data residency — some of our models will touch EU user data.
[00:36] Devon: Okay cool. On SOC2, Redwood maintains Type II, we also have an ISO alignment summary — I will send the cert matrix after. I want to call out that our Hosted API is the fastest to get started, Dedicated gives you reserved capacity with better isolation, and Private gives you a customer-managed control plane for strict residency.
[00:55] Liam: When you say "customer-managed control plane" — do you mean we can keep everything inside our VPC? Like no outbound to Redwood cloud?
[01:03] Devon: For Private deployments, yes — the control plane can be run in your VPC or on-prem. There are variations: the data plane can be fully isolated. For Hosted, we do log ingestion to our telemetry which you can opt out of and forward logs to your SIEM.
[01:19] Maya: And audit logs — what level of granularity? We need to see token-level calls, who triggered model runs, and any parameter changes. Also retention policy — minimum 13 months for us.
[01:31] Devon: We capture request/response metadata, call latency, model id, user id if passed, and can include request hashes. Note: storing full request/response bodies is opt-in and has cost/retention tradeoffs. Defaults are 90 days, but for Dedicated and Private we can extend retention and stream logs to your S3 or Event Hub.
[01:50] Liam: When you say "full bodies opt-in" — does that mean the text input could be preserved?
[01:54] Alicia: Yes, by default we avoid storing user prompt bodies in Hosted unless you enable debugging. For customers who need full logs for auditing we provide a managed option, or for Private you control that entirely.
[02:03] Maya: Good. KMS question: Can we bring our own keys? We use AWS KMS and need to ensure key rotation policies and key access audits. Also legal wants to know if Redwood ever has access to the plaintext model inputs when BYOK is enabled.
[02:16] Devon: BYOK is supported in Dedicated and Private. With BYOK we do envelope encryption — keys live in your KMS, Redwood never has the plaintext key material. For Hosted BYOK there's a mechanism using temporary grants, but for strict compliance we recommend Private so you fully control HSM access.
[02:34] Jenna: Is there an integration guide? We run with an internal KMS wrapper so we'd need the slug for rotations.
[02:39] Devon: Yep, I'll share the KMS integration checklist. It shows steps for key policies, rotation, and example Terraform snippets.
[02:46] Liam: How about SSO? We use Okta with SAML and SCIM for user provisioning. Need SAML for console access and SCIM for user/property sync and roles.
[02:56] Alicia: Redwood supports SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM for provisioning. Roles map to RBAC roles in the Console. We also support OIDC for API auth if you prefer.
[03:07] Maya: On RBAC: can we create custom roles per team, and tie them to model access? We want the marketing team to use only smaller models and legal/dev to access larger ones.
[03:16] Devon: Yes, role-based access control is fairly granular. You can create custom roles, and policies can be scoped to endpoints, models, and even to routes. For Dedicated and Private you get stricter network-level enforcement. There are some UI limits on the Hosted tier but the APIs are the same.
[03:32] Jenna: Any logs for RBAC changes? We need an immutable audit trail when roles change, who changed what.
[03:38] Devon: Absolutely. Role changes, policy edits, and auth events are logged. For compliance we can sign logs and push to your storage.
[03:45] Liam: Do you support FIPS or HSM-backed operations?
[03:49] Alicia: We support HSM-backed keys via integrations with major cloud KMSs and can enable FIPS mode on some deployments. For ultra-regulated environments we recommend Private with an HSM.
[03:59] Maya: Is your SOC2 scoped for both Hosted and Dedicated?
[04:03] Devon: The SOC2 report covers the Redwood platform operations; for Dedicated we provide a separate compliance addendum that covers the reserved capacity environments and responsibilities. For Private, some of the controls shift to you so the report helps but you'd include your deployment controls in your audit.
[04:18] Jenna: Any known gaps for ISO27001?
[04:20] Alicia: We maintain an ISO readiness summary and we can share the gap map. From our side, major items are documented. If you need joint audits we've supported attestation workflows with customers.
[04:31] Liam: Network connectivity — if we want to ensure traffic stays within our peering, do you support VPC peering or private link?
[04:38] Devon: We support both VPC peering and PrivateLink/Direct Connect patterns depending on cloud. Private deployments can be fully within your network and we can disable external egress.
[04:46] Maya: For data residency, we need model inference to run in eu-west-1 exclusively for EU data. Can we enforce geo-routing?
[04:55] Devon: Yep, routing policies can pin requests by region or tenant. For Hosted you can choose region endpoints; for Dedicated/Private you can select region placement.
[05:03] Alicia: Quick interruption — just want to capture that Jenna mentioned legal expects 13 months retention as a minimum.
[05:09] Jenna: Yep. Also, we may need legal to see redaction controls — can Redwood redact PII at ingestion?
[05:16] Devon: We have pre-ingest transformers and customizable redaction pipelines. For high sensitivity you can send only hashes or use client-side tokenization before sending.
[05:25] Liam: About model artifacts and weights — who has access? If we bring a fine-tuned model, can it be kept encrypted at rest and only decrypted on GPUs?
[05:34] Devon: Models at rest are encrypted. For Private and Dedicated the keyspace and access are configurable. Decryption happens in the serving environment; with HSM-backed keys you can enforce strict access policies.
[05:44] Maya: There are latency concerns for decrypt-on-every-request. Does your runtime cache decrypted model in memory or KV cache?
[05:50] Devon: We use an in-memory model cache and optimized key handling so decryption is not per-request. But we can go through performance options in the sizing call.
[05:59] Alicia: Switching to incident response — what does Redwood provide for incident notifications and forensics?
[06:05] Devon: We provide SLA alerts, incident timelines, and we can ship forensic logs on request. For customers with stricter SLAs we offer a dedicated on-call rotation and runbooks.
[06:15] Liam: Are logs tamper-evident? We need chain-of-custody style evidence.
[06:19] Devon: We can sign logs and provide append-only storage options; for Private you can keep logs in your own immutable storage.
[06:26] Maya: Any caveats about multi-tenancy? We need strong tenant isolation, especially for memory/KV cache leakage between tenants.
[06:33] Devon: Memory isolation is enforced at the process/container level. For Hosted we use logical isolation and we do aggressive KV cache partitioning; Dedicated provides stronger physical separation. Private is single-tenant by design. We also run periodic tests for cache leakage.
[06:48] Jenna: Compliance asks for an export of all access logs for the past year during audits — is that feasible?
[06:54] Alicia: Yes, we can export logs, but volume and cost depend on retention policies. We can provide compressed exports and help set up a pipeline to your archival S3.
[07:03] Liam: Can Redwood redact sensitive fields from logs for compliance?
[07:07] Devon: Yes, you can set redaction rules at ingestion and also apply post-processing.
[07:12] Maya: One thing: legal flagged that they want guaranteed key rotation every 90 days. Is that policy enforceable?
[07:18] Devon: If you manage keys in your KMS, rotation policies are yours. For Redwood-managed keys we can configure rotation schedules and provide rotation proofs. But for strict enforcement, BYOK with your KMS is recommended.
[07:30] Jenna: Any third-party audits references you can send?
[07:33] Alicia: Yes, we will send the SOC2 Type II report summary, ISO readiness, and a list of third-party pen test vendors and summaries.
[07:41] Maya: About SCIM — does Redwood support group mappings and attribute sync? We map groups to teams and roles.
[07:47] Devon: SCIM supports group sync and custom attributes. We also support provisioning via Okta and can map to RBAC roles.
[07:55] Liam: Are service principals/audit-only credentials supported for automated jobs?
[07:59] Devon: Yes, we support service principals with scoped API keys and can limit them to read-only or specific model calls. Keys can be rotated automatically.
[08:08] Alicia: Quick note — competitor question: you mentioned you looked at BigCloudAI and a self-hosted route. Anything else we should know about their objections?
[08:16] Maya: BigCloudAI was appealing on price, but their logs and RBAC felt shallow. Self-hosted looked promising for control but we don't have the ops bandwidth.
[08:26] Alicia: Understood. We often see customers choose Dedicated as a middle ground.
[08:30] Jenna: Cost question: If we extend retention to 13 months and store full request bodies, how does that influence pricing?
[08:37] Devon: Storage adds to monthly costs and there's an additional ingestion/retention fee. We can run a cost estimate once you share QPS and average request size.
[08:45] Maya: Ok, we will share QPS in the next two days.
[08:49] Liam: One more thing — can audit logs be forwarded to our Splunk instance?
[08:53] Devon: Yes, we have integrations for Splunk, Elastic, S3, and event hubs.
[08:58] Jenna: For legal, we may need a minimal security design doc showing separation of duties, data handling flows, and authorship of keys.
[09:07] Alicia: We have a standard security pack and a template design doc — I'll send both.
[09:12] Maya: Great. For PII redaction, can we test with a synthetic dataset first?
[09:17] Devon: Absolutely, we can set up a demo tenant with synthetic traffic and show redaction and audit logs.
[09:23] Alicia: Let's recap high level then assign next steps.
[09:27] Alicia: Actions for Redwood: share SOC2/ISO artifacts, KMS integration checklist, SAML/SCIM guide, spin up demo tenant with logs; for Cobalt Hollow: share QPS and data classification, confirm retention and rotation policies.
[09:44] Jenna: Sounds good. One last clarification: in Private mode, does Redwood still have any admin-level access to the cluster?
[09:50] Devon: In Private you control admin plane credentials. Redwood will only have the access you grant for support — and we can do time-boxed support access via ephemeral credentials and audit those sessions.
[09:59] Maya: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[10:01] Alicia: Thanks all. I'll send the materials and follow up with dates for the sizing call.

End of transcript.
